newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil seeks to work with BP, Shell off Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Statoil seeks to work with BP, Shell off Ireland.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday its Irish subsidiary was seeking operatorships in new exploration licences in the deepwater Rockall Trough, west of Ireland.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said it was seeking the operatorships with the Royal/Dutch Shell Group and British Petroleum.
It said the application will be submitted to the Department of Energy next week with awards due in June.
Embracing 615 full and 35 part blocks, the acreage lies in or beyond 1,000 metres of water, 100-300 km from the Irish coast in the Altantic Margin area.
Statoil said the offshore licensing round ranked as the largest in Europe since Norway's first awards in 1965.

"The Rockall Trough is the 'next generation' of exploration on the Irish continental shelf and extends the work we are already doing west of Ireland," said Geirr Haarr, exploration manager for Statoil Ireland.
